text.p: Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest group saw its profits slow by more than six percent last year, after extraordinary items boosted results in 1995, but the media group said it had managed to eliminate its debts in 1996.

Fininvest said on Tuesday net consolidated profits stood at 397.9 billion lire ($234 million), down 6.4 percent from 425.2 billion the previous year, while extraordinary items totalled 1.399 trillion in 1996 against 1.753 trillion previously.

Its net financial position was positive for 213.9 billion lire at December 30, 1996, compared with financial debts of 2.396 trillion the year before, it said in a statement issued after its annual shareholders' meeting.
"The net financial positive has completely reversed," the company said.
The flotations of broadcasting group Mediaset and insurance and financial services company Mediolanum had brought capital gains last year of 1.402 trillion lire.

Fininvest also said it was transferring its controlling stake in Standa, Italy's second largest retailing chain, equal to 80.67 percent of its ordinary capital, to the group's Luxembourg-based financial holding Trefinance SA.
It said Trefinance was buying the stake at a price of 14,000 lire per Standa ordinary share and 3,900 lire per savings share.
The total value of the shares was around 315 billion lire.
Standa ordinary shares stood at 13,840 lire on the Milan bourse at 1230 GMT while savings shares were at 3,500 lire.

The number of ordinary shares transferred by Fininvest and other group subsidiaries totalled 22.35 million, equal to 80.68 percent of the voting rights, and 2.5 million savings shares, or 27.19 percent of total savings shares.
Fininvest said its net financial costs had been reduced to 147.3 billion from 456.1 billion while operating costs were down to 195.4 billion due to reorganisation at the parent company.

Consolidated sales and services revenues were stable at 10.06 trillion, the operating profit stood at 489.1 billion from 368.5 billion previously and the gross operating margin rose to 1.834 trillion from 1.63 trillion before.
Parent company net profits gained to 269.5 billion from 43.4 billion previously.
